main_text.p: illorum scripsit, & consilium adiecit. Incendium hoc Rusticorum non aquâ sed sanguine multorum milliû in bello hoc caesorum, restinctum est.
BELLUM SACRAMENTARIUM continuarunt Saxones, Helvetii, Suevi.
In Saxonia Lutherus Carolostadium, Joannes autem Bugenhagius Ecclesiae VVittebergensis Pastor, Zwinglium, publicis scriptis adoriuntur.

Lutherus statim sub initium anni respondet ad libellos Carolostadii, libro, quem inscribit, Contra caelestes Prophetas (Prophetas enim tum VVittebergae nominabant Anabaptistarum primitias, de revelationibus arcanis & spiritu prophetico gloriantes, Ciconiam, Muncerum, Cellarium, &qui his familiaris fuerat, Carolostadium) Librum illum Lutherus in duas secat partes: primâ de imaginibus, Carolostadio, & Missa agit, affirmaque Imagines in veteri Testamento prohibitas esse, non in novo: Carolostadium à se non fugatum: Missae nomen etiam ab Apostolis, sacramento tributû, & alia: Alterius materies est Eucharistia: ubi primùm exaggerat expositionem Carolostadianâ pronominis Hoc: deinde respondet ad Carolostadii argumenta: aitq; verba, quod pro vobis traditur, hunc habere sensum, corpus quod in pane editis, paulò post, quando non edetur, pro vobis tradetur. Et sicut non scriptû est, accipi-

page.notes: Page is a 16th-century quarto-style page; the printed catchword "accipi-" at the foot is a hyphenated word that continues onto the next page and is kept as the last line. Some letters are worn, e.g. "Muncerum" and "Carolostadianâ" are read as printed. Greek/Hebrew: the pronoun "Ἡ τοῦτο" style Greek glyph before "HOC" appears as a Greek word (τοῦτο) in the printed text; it is shown here as the Latin-letter gloss "Hoc" and should be checked against the scan.
